questions.q: Why does the book say exercise cannot undo long sitting?
a: Six hours of sitting harms health even if you work out after
Exercise burns too few calories to matter for health
Working out increases appetite and leads to weight gain
Sitting stretches muscles in ways exercise cannot fix
questions.why: Lesson 1 says that if you sit six hours a day, even two hours of exercise afterward will not reverse the damage.

questions.q: How long should you avoid sitting at a stretch?
a: No longer than an hour
No longer than two hours
No longer than three hours
No longer than thirty minutes
questions.why: Lesson 1 gives one simple rule: do not sit for longer than an hour.

questions.q: What three traits make added sugar behave like a drug?
a: It releases dopamine, increases cravings and builds tolerance
It raises energy, lowers appetite and improves sleep
It causes headaches, nausea and rapid weight loss
It is addictive only when eaten with other sweets
questions.why: Lesson 2 says sugar gives a dopamine high, makes you want more and builds tolerance, so it should be treated like an illegal drug.

questions.q: Why does hitting snooze leave you groggy?
a: The alarm wakes you as you sink back into deep sleep
The extra sleep confuses your body's internal clock
You lose the habit of waking at a fixed time
The room is too bright by the time you wake again
questions.why: Lesson 3 explains that a second alarm catches you just as you re-enter deep sleep, which makes you tired rather than rested.

questions.q: How much refined sugar does the summary say the average person eats in a year?
a: Their own body weight
Half their body weight
Twice their body weight
About ten kilograms
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the amount matches your body weight in refined white sugar, pictured as a statue of yourself eaten daily.
